title: Video by invention
description:
Maintaining a steady throttle for long periods can fatigue a rider’s wrist, especially during highway cruising. An aftermarket throttle lock provides a simple mechanical way to hold the grip in position without constant pressure from the rider’s hand.

The device works through a small locking mechanism activated by a dedicated button. When pressed, it creates controlled friction against the throttle tube, allowing the engine input to remain consistent while the rider relaxes their grip or adjusts hand position.

Control can be restored instantly using the separate release button or by manually rolling the throttle. This ensures the motorcycle continues to respond normally while offering a practical comfort aid for extended riding conditions.

title: Video by github.awesome
description:
What happens to your password manager if you’re gone tomorrow? After concussions and a documentary about memory loss, a developer built ReMemory: a cryptographic dead man’s switch using Shamir’s Secret Sharing. You encrypt files, split the key into five shares, and give them to friends. Any three can recover it; two reveal zero information. Each share is an offline HTML file—no servers, installs, or internet—built to work even decades later. 

https://github.com/eljojo/rememory

#github #opensource

title: Video by deeplearnai
description:
Spam calls are one of the most annoying problems on the internet era. But surprisingly, a U.S. law from 1991 might allow you to earn up to $1,500 for each illegal robocall.

The problem is that most robocallers hide behind fake names, spoofed phone numbers, and anonymous operations, making it almost impossible for consumers to identify them.

That’s where technology - and increasingly AI - comes in.

Tools like DoNotPay created a virtual credit card system designed to uncover the real identity of spam callers. When a robocaller tries to sell you something, you give them the virtual card. When they attempt to process the payment, the payment network reveals the business name, address, and phone number behind the call.

That information can then be used to automatically generate legal claims under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act.

One user reportedly turned this into a full-time strategy, earning nearly $100,000 from robocall lawsuits.

AI isn’t just automating tasks - it’s helping people fight back.
